note: Teaching text, clarifying questions, inferred constraints and own examples. Inferred, not official. Examples are small generated inputs with outputs from the independent references in oracles.py.

clarifyingQuestions: May x be merged into a value that is not present?
Does the final array have to keep at least two values?
Is an already contiguous array answered with 0?
hints: Merging values never helps unless their occurrence ranges overlap.
Cut the array at every index where no value occurs on both sides; each piece must end up as one value.
Each operation removes one distinct value, so the answer is distinct values minus the number of pieces; find pieces with the last occurrence of every value.
invariants: every piece is closed: no value occurs both inside and outside it
the answer never exceeds distinct values minus 1
chooseWhen: Partitioning a sequence into value-closed pieces
tradeoffs: Last-occurrence sweep is linear; explicit union-find over overlapping ranges is equivalent but heavier
hack2hire:6a31cf175117d1b543567dcc.variantLabel: Single variant: fewest relabel operations to make every value contiguous

constraints: timestamps are decimal integers 0 to 1e9, non-decreasing
a sell never exceeds the shares held
clarifyingQuestions: Which purchased shares does a sell consume?
Is the tax computed per sell or on the net profit of all sells?
How should the tax be formatted?
Can a sell exceed the shares currently held?
hints: Selling the most expensive shares first makes each sell's profit as small as possible.
Keep the lots in a max-heap keyed by buy price.

For a sell, pop lots until the amount is covered (push back a partial remainder), sum (sell price - lot price) * shares, and add max(0, profit) to an integer total of tenths; format total // 10 and total % 10.
invariants: the heap holds exactly the unsold shares
the integer profit total never goes negative
chooseWhen: Lot matching with a priority rule
tradeoffs: A heap gives O(log n) per lot; re-sorting is simpler but quadratic
hack2hire:6796992ab10bc587828f27ae.variantLabel: Single variant: total tax when sells consume the costliest shares first

clarifyingQuestions: Can latencies repeat?
How are pairs ordered, and is each pair written smaller value first?
hints: In sorted order the closest pair is always adjacent.
Sort a copy and compute the minimum gap between neighbours.
Walk the neighbours again and keep every pair whose gap equals the minimum.
invariants: pairs come out in ascending order of their first value
every reported pair has gap d
tradeoffs: Sorting costs O(n log n); a counting approach needs a small value range
hack2hire:69cac664ff3ebde766ced9a5.variantLabel: Single variant: all value pairs at the minimum difference

clarifyingQuestions: Can a denomination be used more than once?
When is the answer -1?
Do denominations above max matter?
hints: If the chosen coins can pay every amount up to r, a new coin c <= r + 1 extends that to r + c.
Greedily add the largest denomination not above r + 1.
The same denomination repeats until the next one becomes usable or max is reached; compute that repetition count with one division.
invariants: after every pick all amounts 1..r are payable
r strictly increases
chooseWhen: Covering a range with subset sums
tradeoffs: The greedy with jumps runs per denomination; simulating coin by coin can take max steps
hack2hire:67803efe6fee41e51af73ddc.variantLabel: Single variant: smallest coin multiset covering 1..max

clarifyingQuestions: Can more bundles be bought than either requirement?
Can x or y be 0?
hints: Fix the number of bundles b; the rest is bought singly.
cost(b) = b * bundleCost + max(0, x - b) * edgeCost + max(0, y - b) * inputCost is piecewise linear with breaks at x and y.
The minimum is at b = 0, b = min(x, y) or b = max(x, y).
invariants: every evaluated plan satisfies both requirements
tradeoffs: Checking breakpoints is O(1); scanning all b is simple but linear in the requirements
hack2hire:6a74eeddd713d873ca7a8195.variantLabel: Single variant: cheapest mix of single items and bundles

clarifyingQuestions: Must all units move the same way?
Is the cost per unit per link?
hints: With clockwise moves only, the flow on link i equals c + prefix_i for some constant c >= -min(prefix).
Total cost is the sum of link flows, minimised by the smallest valid c.
Counterclockwise is the mirror image with c' - prefix_i; return the cheaper direction.
invariants: link flows are non-negative
flow conservation holds at every warehouse
chooseWhen: Circular balancing with a direction restriction
tradeoffs: The prefix formula is linear; trying every zero-flow link is quadratic
hack2hire:6a31cd3f5117d1b543567dbe.variantLabel: Single variant: one-direction rebalancing on a ring

constraints: the edges form a tree when directions are ignored
clarifyingQuestions: Is the input guaranteed to be a tree?
Should the root also be reported?
hints: Count reversals for one root with a traversal.
Moving the root from u to its neighbour v only changes the edge between them.
If the edge points u -> v the cost grows by 1, otherwise it shrinks by 1; take the minimum over all nodes, iteratively to avoid deep recursion.
invariants: cost(v) = cost(u) + 1 when the edge is u -> v and cost(u) - 1 when it is v -> u
tradeoffs: Rerooting is linear; per-root search is quadratic
hack2hire:69f1384f96981f58ae1f7687.variantLabel: Single variant: best root for an oriented tree

clarifyingQuestions: Must the neighbouring robots be adjacent, or anywhere on the same row or column?
Are positions distinct?
hints: Only extremes matter: a robot has someone above it unless it is the topmost on its column.
Record the min and max y per x and the min and max x per y.
Count robots strictly between the extremes in both directions.
invariants: a robot at a column or row extreme is never idle
tradeoffs: Hash maps give linear time; sorting rows and columns is an alternative
hack2hire:67888093402dc47b67a14948.variantLabel: Single variant: robots surrounded on four sides

constraints: names are distinct, 1 to 12 characters from a-z, 0-9 and _
clarifyingQuestions: Which queries does the class answer: offset by name, field by offset, total size?
What is returned for an unknown field or an offset past the end?
Can fields be added or removed after construction, and do later fields shift?
hints: The offset of a field is the sum of sizes of the live fields before it.
Keep sizes in a Fenwick tree indexed by insertion slot; a removed field becomes size 0.
fieldAt walks down the Fenwick tree to the first slot whose prefix sum exceeds the offset.
invariants: the Fenwick total equals totalSize()
live fields keep their insertion order
tradeoffs: A Fenwick tree makes every query logarithmic; a plain list is simpler but linear per call
hack2hire:69cda519ff3ebde766cee834.variantLabel: Single variant: packed field offsets with append and remove

constraints: c is one character from a-z, A-Z or 0-9; comparison is case-sensitive
clarifyingQuestions: Is the empty stream a palindrome?
Is the comparison case-sensitive, and which characters can arrive?
How often is isPalindrome called relative to track?
hints: Rechecking the whole string per query is quadratic; a rolling hash is fast but can collide.
Track the longest palindromic suffix of the stream as it grows.
A palindromic tree updates that suffix in amortised O(1) per character; the stream is a palindrome when the suffix length equals the stream length.
invariants: the tracked suffix is the longest palindromic suffix of the stream
suffix links point to strictly shorter palindromes
tradeoffs: The eertree is exact; polynomial hashing is simpler but probabilistic
hack2hire:68d89bb279db2fbcd7d7db16.variantLabel: Single variant: is the whole stream a palindrome

clarifyingQuestions: What is the equation: ABC + DEF = GHI?
Do ABC + DEF and DEF + ABC count as different assignments?
Is there any input, or is the answer a constant?
hints: Work from the units column: C + F gives I and a carry.
Once two addend digits are chosen, the sum digit of that column is forced; reject it if used or fixed differently.
Recurse to the tens and hundreds columns; the hundreds column must not carry.
invariants: each digit 1..9 is used at most once along a search path
the carry is 0 or 1
tradeoffs: Column-wise backtracking prunes early; brute-force permutations are 9! checks
hack2hire:6907b46fe1919109b6df119a.variantLabel: Single variant: count digit assignments with ABC + DEF = GHI (pattern extension)

constraints: letters a-z, A-Z and single spaces; words are non-empty
clarifyingQuestions: Is "y" a vowel?
Does a moved capital letter stay capital?
Are there punctuation or extra rules, as in Goat Latin?
hints: Handle each word independently.
Check the first letter against the vowels in both cases.
Vowel: word + "way"; consonant: word[1:] + word[0] + "ay"; join with spaces.
invariants: the output has as many words as the input
tradeoffs: Splitting is clearest; a single character scan avoids temporary lists

clarifyingQuestions: Can fractional shares be bought?
Does leftover cash count towards the value?
How should the value be rounded and formatted?
hints: Each dollar spent on security i returns S_i / P_i of future value.
Buy in decreasing S / P order, comparing ratios by cross-multiplication.
Buy whole maximum lots while they fit, then the affordable fraction of the next security; keep the result exact until the final rounding.
invariants: spent funds never exceed funds
the fractional purchase, if any, is the last one
tradeoffs: Greedy by ratio is optimal for fractional shares; whole shares would need a different algorithm
hack2hire:67cd196d3363b83a81fc99a7.variantLabel: Single variant: fractional knapsack over securities

constraints: every child id is in idList and has exactly one parent; no cycles
names are 1 to 10 characters from letters, digits and _
clarifyingQuestions: How is the path printed: joined names, a list, a leading slash?
What if targetId does not exist?
Can the forest be deep?
hints: Each folder has at most one parent.
Build a child-to-parent map and an id-to-name map.
Walk parents from targetId to the top, collecting names, then reverse and join; iterate, do not recurse.
invariants: the walk visits each ancestor once and stops at a top-level folder
tradeoffs: A parent map answers one query in path length; a top-down search needs the whole forest

constraints: item names are 1 to 20 characters: letters and digits with single inner spaces, no commas
dates are yyyy-mm-dd with year 2000 to 2099, month 01 to 12, day 01 to 28
clarifyingQuestions: What does a query look like?
Is a date unique per item or across the log?
Which price applies between two log dates, and before the first one?
hints: ISO dates compare correctly as strings.
Split each entry on its last two ", " separators, since names may contain spaces.
Sort each item's (date, price) list and binary-search the last date <= the query date.
invariants: each item's list is sorted by date
answers are -1 exactly when no entry is on or before the query date
tradeoffs: Sorting plus binary search handles unsorted logs; a scan is simpler but O(n) per query
hack2hire:68f68778a269f53ea0eff91d.variantLabel: Single variant: price as of a date per item

clarifyingQuestions: What do the queries return before any update?
Does a replaced price still count for the maximum or minimum?
Is "latest" the newest timestamp or the newest call?
hints: Keep the current price per timestamp in a hash map and remember the largest timestamp.
Push every update into a max-heap and a min-heap as (price, timestamp).
On a query pop heap tops whose price no longer matches the map for their timestamp; the remaining top is the answer.
invariants: the map holds exactly one price per recorded timestamp
every live record has an entry in both heaps
chooseWhen: Aggregates over a corrected time series
tradeoffs: Lazy heaps give logarithmic amortised time; a sorted multiset would also delete eagerly
hack2hire:68aceb961bf7d2097f647f62.variantLabel: Single variant: latest, max and min price with corrections
